standard_prerequisites: Cartesian products and the product induction principle allowing a function on a product of function types to be defined on pairs.
The characterization of paths in product types and its uniqueness corollary (the retained context).
Function extensionality: pointwise identified functions are identified as functions.
The uniqueness principle for functions: a pair of functions applied pointwise is judgmentally the pair of the pointwise parts.
core_obligations: Construct the quasi-inverse sending a pair of functions to their pointwise pairing.

Prove the first round-trip identification: pairing the projections of f pointwise is pointwise identified with f by the product uniqueness principle, hence identified as functions by function extensionality.
Prove the second round-trip identification: the pointwise projections of the pairing of g and h are judgmentally the pair of g and h.
Conclude that the projection map is an equivalence.
proof_roadmap: Define the inverse: send (g, h) to the function x maps to (g(x), h(x)); the author notes this uses product induction on the pair of function types to reduce to the case of a pair.

First direction: the round-trip on f yields the pointwise pairing of the projections of f; by the product uniqueness principle (from the product path characterization, the retained context) each pointwise instance is identified with f(x); by function extensionality the functions are identified.
Second direction: the round-trip on (g, h) yields the pair of pointwise parts, which is judgmentally (g, h) by the uniqueness principle for functions.
Conclude the equivalence, which is the universal property of the product in its homotopical form.
difficulty_reason: The argument is short but combines three principles (product path characterization, function extensionality, judgmental uniqueness for pairings) whose interplay must be stated precisely.
